identity.name: S. P. APPARELS LIMITED
identity.industry: Apparel & Textiles / Export-Driven Garment Manufacturing with Integrated Verticals

summary.oneLiner: Strong Q2 performance driven by retail and SPUK turning EBITDA-positive, Sri Lanka scaling to INR 50cr annual revenue, and 24% export growth offset U.S. tariff headwinds; the consolidated EBITDA margin of 14.9% and INR 400cr order book signal sustainable turnaround, with FY27 revenue guidance of INR 2,000cr now credible.

one-line thesis: Strong Q2 performance driven by retail and SPUK turning EBITDA-positive, Sri Lanka scaling to INR 50cr annual revenue, and 24% export growth offset U.S. tariff headwinds; the consolidated EBITDA margin of 14.9% and INR 400cr order book signal sustainable turnaround, with FY27 revenue guidance of INR 2,000cr now credible.
financial scorecard: revenue: +9.2% YoY (consol); EBITDA/margin: +28.1% YoY, 14.9% (consol); PAT (rptd): +58.4% YoY, INR 34.7cr; PAT (normalized): +58.4% YoY (no major one-offs); order book: INR 400cr (incl. INR 50cr expected in 1 week); net debt: INR 303cr (consol), ECB $6m for Sri Lanka
guidance: revenue growth: INR 2,000cr consolidated FY27; margin: 15% EBITDA margin target; order inflow: 100M pieces annual capacity by FY27; capex/commissioning: minimal H2FY26 capex (INR 4-5cr); FY27 capex INR 10cr (maintenance only); FY28 to see 15-20% capacity addition
segment / subsidiary detail: Garment: 18.9M pieces exported (24% YoY), 83% util, 3-4 new EU customers; Young Brand: INR 84cr rev, 14.9% EBITDA margin, Sivakasi capacity reduced to 30-40 machines pending U.S. tariff clarity; SPUK: INR 18cr rev, INR 1.1cr EBITDA (positive vs loss last year); Retail: INR 21.7cr rev, INR 53L EBITDA (first positive), Crocodile INR 16cr, Angel & Rocket INR 5cr, D2C up 200%
growth verticals / optionality: Sri Lanka to contribute INR 100cr+ in FY27; U.K. FTA (expected Mar 2026) to boost volumes; Angel & Rocket D2C to scale to INR 4-5cr/month with capex; potential for U.S. customer in Sri Lanka by FY27
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin guidance of 15% consolidated; U.S. tariff at 50% absorbed via supply chain sharing (no new margin pressure in Q3/Q4); gross margin improved 7% in retail due to product mix and overhead reduction; Sri Lanka cost advantage enables margin resilience
capex / expansion: H2FY26: INR 4-5cr (maintenance); FY27: INR 10cr (maintenance); no major capex until FY28; 8,000 machines installed by FY27 (6k India + 2k Sri Lanka); next capex wave (1k-2k machines) planned for FY28
capital allocation: Prioritizing debt reduction (net debt INR 303cr); retail division seeking strategic financial partner; no dividend policy mentioned; capex deferred to stabilize operations before FY28 expansion
risks & watch-items: U.S. 50% tariff persistence (risk of 50% business shift out of India); delayed U.K. FTA implementation; Sri Lanka operational ramp-up delays; retail growth dependent on D2C marketing spend
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and pragmatic; clear focus on stabilization over expansion; transparent on U.S. tariff risks; retail turnaround framed as structural, not cyclical; strong conviction on Sri Lanka and U.K. FTA as long-term levers
non-obvious takeaways: Retail’s EBITDA positivity is largely from overhead cuts (6-7%) and gross margin lift (7%), not revenue growth; SPUK’s ROCE at 4-5% implies low capital efficiency, yet management expects margin-driven improvement; 100M pieces capacity assumes 93% utilisation — aggressive but credible given order book

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
